trick: A bigger model reviews the code: does Opus catch more than a fresh Haiku?
source_note: 24 Oct rerun on the four-bug project, approved by Sebi 24 Oct in chat ("rerunning days 42 to 50 on it with 18 runs a side"): base/subtrack (frozen v3, fixtures/subtrack/frozen/v3), task m5-weekly-plans (one ticket, four hidden traps B1-B4 plus core; plain Haiku 4.5 passed all four in 3 of 10 calibration runs, tasks/m5-weekly-plans/CALIBRATION.md). Same trick and sides as tricks/d42-v1 (the t2/h2 version, kept with its runs in runs/d42-v1; its source_note describes the trick in full). 18 runs a side, Haiku 4.5. Both sides get the same allowed_tools_extra (`npm test`, `npm run test`), as in the calibration pilot tricks/pilot-m5fix-3; the CLI runs through the lab's existing `node *` allowance (`node bin/subtrack.js ...`). Per-bug map per side: python3 tricks/m5-common/bugs_map.py runs/d42 (B1-B4, all four, cheat, from each row's BUGS fields). Changes: none to the three-call design, models or prompts. The snap overlay and check_step1.py are copied unchanged into this folder (byte-identical to v1's). count_steps.py here also reports, per trap (B1-B4, core, all four), the runs passing it after the writer's call and at the end, and those fixed or broken by review+fix; its labelling sheet (--review-step 1 --sheet) adds the traps the first call failed (first_call_failing), so real-bug = the issue names a trap the step-1 code fails. Timeout 30 min for the three calls, as v1.
tasks_note: 24 Oct rerun: m5-weekly-plans only (base/subtrack); runs is per task, so 18 a side.
model_note: Set 23 Oct after the E1 pilot: current Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 passed 20 of 20 pilot runs, so a Sonnet writer would leave nothing to review. Writer and fixer are the Season 2 model (Haiku 4.5) on both sides; the fresh reviewer is Opus 5.5 (with) vs Haiku 4.5 (without). Ids confirmed by one-line claude -p calls (runs/pilot-e1-models/models.txt).
